#### What this PR does / why we need it:
The scheduler framework instantiation currently handles defaulting the weights of Score plugins, as well as checking that the total weight is not more than the maximum. This PR moves it to the API defaulting itself to catch this earlier and be more secure.

@damemi could you inform me about what is wrong in my implementation here. And what should be a better code design for the purpose.
@damemi Could you please guide me a little about what is wrong in this PR and how to make a better solution for moving scheduler Score plugin weight defaulting to API.

Hi @NikhilSharmaWe, sorry about the delay. As we mentioned in the issue for this (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/106426) @kerthcet already expressed that they were working on a fix for this. Perhaps you would be interested in collaborating together, which may help you learn some more about the internals of these files.

To answer your question here, your changes are missing on some details. First, we don't need to move the entire `frameworkImpl` struct to this package -- most of those fields are only used in the framework runtime package, so those fields aren't relevant to defaulting or validation. Additionally, your `ScorePlugin` function looks okay (seems to be the same logic copied here), but it is never actually called anywhere. The key to these defaulting functions is that they are called against the type itself, and this call stack is usually initialized in one of the `SetDefaults_...` functions you see elsewhere in this file. 

As a side note, it's also important to remember that when we move logic like this from one area to another you need to delete the old logic (in this case, the code from framework runtime).

You might also want to play with making changes like this in [validation](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7ee6a9c8a4ebfa246b93b8ec7f61151f8af2cec0/pkg/scheduler/apis/config/validation/validation.go#L41) rather than defaulting. Test your changes in a local cluster if you can by building the scheduler code and deploying it (I have a [blog post on how to do that](https://mikeda.me/how-to-build-custom-kubernetes-control-plane-images-and-test-them-with-kind/), if it helps). We want to either see an error with plugins that have no weight (validation), or have weights automatically filled in (defaulting, what you have here). I think in this case, since this logic is really checking for an overflow, we want a validation error.

I would try to sync up with @kerthcet to work together on this, their experience will be helpful especially if there is already another PR in the works that you can learn from. Hope this helps!

`The key to these defaulting functions is that they are called against the type itself, and this call stack is usually initialized in one of the SetDefaults_... functions you see elsewhere in this file.`

@damemi 

- So, do I need to change the function name and initialize it with `SetDefaults_`, but what difference will it make ?

- Also what do you mean by `The key to these defaulting functions is that they are called against the type itself` ?

Could you please elaborate.

@NikhilSharmaWe just changing the name of the function won't do anything, you have to make sure it is actually called from somewhere. For example, place a call to it inside [`SetDefaults_KubeSchedulerConfiguration()`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/7ee6a9c8a4ebfa246b93b8ec7f61151f8af2cec0/pkg/scheduler/apis/config/v1beta2/defaults.go#L141). That's what I meant by the fact that these functions need to be called on the type

issue_context.title: Move scheduler Score plugin weight defaulting to API
issue_context.body:
The scheduler framework instantiation currently handles defaulting the weights of Score plugins, as well as checking that the total weight is not more than the maximum:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9dc0489/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L292-L306

this should be moved to the API defaulting itself to catch this earlier and be more secure
/sig scheduling
/kind feature

</details>

I can give some help. 
/assign
@damemi I would like to collaborate. Could you please elaborate and tell in **what files** the changes should be made for handling the weight of Score Plugins in API Defaulting.

@NikhilSharmaWe it looks like @kerthcet has already offered to work on this, but if you would like to collaborate on it feel free. The code in question is located in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9dc0489/pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework.go#L292-L306, and we are interested in moving it to the actual API defaulting sections, probably https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9dc0489c1ae3540453d94348efcc536585c31805/pkg/scheduler/apis/config/v1beta2/defaults.go

Yes, I'm working on this issue also, but I haven't push commits yet for I still have some questions, let's discuss about it 
 here. Correct me if any mis-understandings.

Since we'll merge out-of-tree plugins [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go#L236-L239), I think move the codes to `default.go` will miss some plugins. 

And I prefer to move the code [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/scheduler/profile/profile.go#L88-L118), as we have already validate the `QueueSort` Plugins here. WDYT @damemi

> @kerthcet I don't think out-of-tree plugins will miss the validation if we move it to API. This is going to be agnostic of the specific plugin types, validating that there is just a weight set for each score plugin and that those weights aren't more than the max score. Another possible location could be here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9dc0489c1ae3540453d94348efcc536585c31805/pkg/scheduler/apis/config/validation/validation.go
> 
> I also don't think moving the code to `profile.go` is what we want either. We're validating `QueueSort` plugins in that spot because we need to check across each individual profile("framework") to make sure there are no conflicts. The reason that check is in that spot is because that's after each framework/profile has been initialized. But, we could check the score weights on individual profiles as they're created. Does that make sense?
> 
yes, I double-checked the code and I found I misunderstood the intention of function `merge()`. Thanks for your explanations, I'll push a commit tomorrow and some tests are needed too.

hi @damemi , I found it's easy to handle plugins in `KubeSchedulerProfile.Plugins.Score.Enabled` since all the plugins are implements of `ScoreExtensionPoint` , however , we can not make sure what extension point these plugins implemented in `KubeSchedulerProfile.Plugins.MultiPoint.Enabled`, for only score plugins using these weights. do you have any idea?

@kerthcet that is the challenge with this, and I'm open to suggestions on how we could implement it. You might have to look into doing a similar loop to try to cast all of the MultiPoint plugins to a ScorePlugin, and if that succeeds then check for the weights.
thanks, I'll have a try then.
@kerthcet any updates or progress on this?
Sorry, I just return from holidays and I talked with @NikhilSharmaWe , he is free to continue his work and I can provide some help if needed.
